pages.c05-p01: Demonstrate understanding of and use the following: data validation, including presence, length, type and format checks
pages.c05-p02: Demonstrate understanding of and use the following: detection and correction techniques for syntax, execution and logic errors
pages.c05-p03: Demonstrate understanding of and use the following: simple error trapping techniques

q.q: What is validation?
o: A check carried out by a person, comparing the data entered with the original document
An automatic check, carried out by the program, that input data is sensible and obeys set rules before it is used
A check that the data entered is exactly correct and matches the real-world value
A process that finds and removes logic errors from a program before it is released
q.why: Validation is automatic and checks data is sensible, complete and within limits. It cannot prove data is correct.

q.q: What does the phrase "garbage in, garbage out" mean?
o: A computer processes exactly what it is given, so wrong data in gives wrong results out
A program that contains errors will always delete the data it is given
Data that is no longer needed should be removed from the system regularly
Any data entered into a computer is automatically corrected before output
q.why: Computers cannot tell that data is wrong; validation reduces the bad data that gets in.

q.q: Which three things does validation check about input data?
o: That it is accurate, up to date and correct
That it is complete, within the set limits and sensible
That it is encrypted, backed up and secure
That it is compiled, tested and debugged
q.why: Validation checks that data is complete (nothing missing), within limits and sensible.

q.q: Which check makes sure a password has at least 8 characters?
o: Range check
Presence check
Length check
Type check
q.why: A length check counts characters. A range check tests a value between limits.

q.q: Which check is "the postcode must start with BT"?
o: Range check
Presence check
Length check
Format check
q.why: It checks the pattern of the data.

q.q: Which check makes sure the surname box has not been left blank?
o: Length check
Presence check
Format check
Type check
q.why: A presence check makes sure something has been entered.

q.q: Which check makes sure that a quantity entered is a whole number?
o: Type check
Range check
Format check
Presence check
q.why: A type check makes sure the data is the correct data type.

q.q: A bowling alley allows between 10 and 40 frames. Which check makes sure the number entered is within these limits?
o: Length check
Type check
Format check
Range check
q.why: A range check tests whether a value lies between limits.

q.q: Which four validation checks are named in the CCEA specification?
o: Presence, length, range and format
Range, type, format and lookup
Length, type, range and check digit
Presence, length, type and format
q.why: The specification names presence, length, type and format. Range checks appear in past papers too, so learn all five.

q.q: Which C# condition is True for valid data in a presence check on surname?
o: surname == ""
surname.Length >= 8
surname != ""
surname.Contains("@")
q.why: surname != "" is True when something has been entered. == "" would be True for a blank, invalid entry.

q.q: Which C# condition is True for valid data in a length check that a password has at least 8 characters?
o: password.Length > 8
password.Length >= 8
password.Length <= 8
password != "8"
q.why: At least 8 includes 8, so >= is needed; > 8 would wrongly reject an 8-character password.

q.q: Which C# condition is True for valid data in a range check of frames from 10 to 40?
o: frames >= 10 || frames <= 40
frames > 10 && frames < 40
frames <= 10 && frames >= 40
frames >= 10 && frames <= 40
q.why: Both limits must hold (AND) and inclusive limits need >= and <=. The OR version is true for any number.

q.q: Which C# condition is True for valid data in a format check that an email contains @?
o: email.Length == 1
email != "@"
email.IndexOf("@") == -1
email.Contains("@")
q.why: Contains returns True if @ is present. IndexOf returning −1 means it is missing.

q.q: What is a validation loop?
o: A loop that repeats the input, with an error message, for as long as the data is invalid
A loop that repeats the input a fixed number of times, then accepts the last value
A loop that checks every element of an array is sorted into order
A loop that tests the program with normal, boundary and erroneous data
q.why: A validation loop keeps asking until the input passes.

q.q: Why should a validation loop use WHILE rather than FOR?
o: A FOR loop cannot contain an IF statement inside it
A WHILE loop always runs exactly once, so the input is checked once
You do not know in advance how many attempts the user will need
A FOR loop would convert the input into an integer automatically
q.why: A FOR loop repeats a set number of times; validation needs to repeat until valid.

q.q: A program asks for an age from 11 to 18. Which condition keeps a validation loop running while the age is invalid?
o: age < 11 || age > 18
age < 11 && age > 18
age > 11 || age < 18
q.why: An age is invalid if it is below 11 OR above 18. No number can be both, so && would never loop; the third option describes valid data.

q.q: A pupil writes the validation loop while (age < 11 && age > 18). What will happen when the user types 25?
o: The loop will run for ever, because 25 can never satisfy the condition
The loop will not run, so 25 is accepted, because no number can be both below 11 and above 18
The loop will run once, show an error and then accept 25
The program will crash, because && cannot be used in a WHILE condition
q.why: The && condition is always False, so invalid values pass straight through.

q.q: In a validation loop, why does the WHILE condition describe invalid data?
o: The condition must be False on the first test so the loop always runs once
The loop must keep repeating while the data is invalid and stop once it is valid
C# WHILE loops can only test for values that are out of range
The error message is shown only when the condition is False
q.why: The loop body (error and re-input) should run while the data is invalid.

q.q: In a 'write a validation loop' question, which of these usually earns a mark?
o: An error message before the first input
A FOR loop that runs three times
An error message and a re-input inside the loop
An output of the valid value inside the loop
q.why: Marks go for the first input, a correct WHILE condition, an error message and re-input inside the loop, and the right variable names.

q.q: What does int.TryParse(Console.ReadLine(), out frames) return if the user types "twelve"?
o: true, and frames is set to 12
false, and the program crashes
false, and frames is set to 0
true, and frames is set to 0
q.why: TryParse returns false (setting frames to 0) if the text is not a whole number, so letters never crash the program.

q.q: What does int.TryParse(Console.ReadLine(), out frames) do if the user types "25"?
o: Returns false and puts 25 in frames
Returns 25 and leaves frames unchanged
Returns true and leaves frames as 0
Returns true and puts 25 in frames
q.why: TryParse attempts the conversion and puts the number in frames when it succeeds.

q.q: Why is int.TryParse useful for a type check?
o: It converts any text, including letters, into a whole number
It tests whether text is a whole number without crashing the program if it is not
It checks that a whole number is within a given range
It removes any spaces from the input before it is stored
q.why: It returns true or false instead of throwing an exception, so letters never crash the program.

q.q: In a loop such as while (!isNumber || frames < 10 || frames > 40), what does !isNumber test?
o: Whether the input was not a whole number
Whether the input was a whole number
Whether frames is zero
Whether the loop has run before
q.why: ! is NOT, so !isNumber is True when TryParse failed.

q.q: A pupil code must be two letters then three digits, such as EK204. Which type of check is this?
o: Length check only
Format check
Range check
Type check
q.why: It checks that the data matches a pattern. The code also includes a length check, but the pattern is a format check.

q.q: In the pupil code check, why is code.Length == 5 tested before char.IsDigit(code[4])?
o: The length must be tested last, otherwise the letters are not checked
char.IsDigit only works on strings of exactly five characters
It makes no difference, as C# tests all parts of an && condition anyway
&& stops at the first False, so code[4] is never read from a string that is too short
q.why: Short-circuit evaluation protects against reading an index that does not exist.

q.q: What does char.IsDigit(code[2]) test?
o: Whether the character at index 2 of code is a digit
Whether code contains exactly 2 digits
Whether the third character of code is a letter
Whether code is a whole number
q.why: char.IsDigit and char.IsLetter each test a single character.

q.q: A user types EKO04 (with the letter O instead of a zero) for a pupil code that must be two letters then three digits. What happens?
o: The format check rejects it, because the third character is not a digit
The format check accepts it, because the code is five characters long
The length check rejects it, because O is not a valid character
The program crashes, because O cannot be converted to a number
q.why: char.IsDigit('O') is false, so the code fails the format check.

q.q: Why is the pupil code converted with ToUpper() before being checked?
o: So that lower-case and upper-case entries are treated the same
So that the digits are converted into letters
So that the length of the code is increased to 5
So that the code is stored as a number rather than text
q.why: Converting to upper case makes the check case-insensitive.

q.q: A user types an age of 21 instead of 22. Why does validation not catch this?
o: 21 is sensible and obeys all the rules, so it passes; validation cannot prove data is correct
The validation loop only runs once, so the second attempt is not checked
Validation only checks text, not numbers
Validation checks data only after it has been stored in a file
q.why: Valid does not mean correct; validation only checks data is reasonable.

q.q: A pupil writes "Validation makes sure the data entered is accurate." Why is this wrong?
o: Validation only checks data that has already been processed by the program
Validation is carried out by a person, so it is often inaccurate
Validation only works on whole numbers, not on text
Validation only checks that data is reasonable and follows rules; sensible data can still be wrong
q.why: Examiners regularly see this claim; validation reduces bad data but cannot remove it completely.

q.q: A booking form needs a date of birth to be entered in the form dd/mm/yyyy. Which check is most suitable?
o: Presence check
Length check
Range check
Format check
q.why: The data must match a pattern.

q.q: A school wants to make sure that a mark entered for a test is between 0 and 100. Which check should be used?
o: Format check
Length check
Presence check
Range check
q.why: The value must lie between limits.

q.q: A mobile phone number must contain exactly 11 characters. Which check is most suitable?
o: Range check
Type check
Length check
Presence check
q.why: A length check tests the number of characters. A range check would treat it as a value.

q.q: A club membership form must not be submitted without an email address. Which check makes sure one is entered?
o: Presence check
Format check
Length check
Type check
q.why: Something must be entered, which is a presence check. A format check would test for @.

q.q: A program asks for the number of tickets and must reject "two" or "2.5". Which check is this?
o: Format check
Range check
Presence check
Type check
q.why: The data must be the correct data type, a whole number.

q.q: Which validation loop is correct for a password of at least 8 characters?
o: while (password.Length < 8) { error message; input password again }
while (password.Length >= 8) { error message; input password again }
for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) { error message; input password again }
while (password.Length < 8) { input password again } then error message
q.why: The loop runs while invalid (fewer than 8), with the error and re-input inside it.

q.q: What is a syntax error?
o: Code that runs to the end but gives the wrong result because the reasoning is wrong
Code that breaks the grammar rules of the language, so it cannot be translated and will not run
Code that translates and starts, but crashes while it is running
Data entered by the user that does not follow the validation rules
q.why: Syntax errors stop the program compiling. The other options describe logic and execution errors.

q.q: What is an execution (run-time) error?
o: The program will not translate because it breaks the language rules
The program runs to the end but produces the wrong output
The program translates and starts, but crashes while it is running
The program runs correctly but too slowly
q.why: An execution error crashes a running program with an exception message.

q.q: What is a logic error?
o: The program will not translate, because a rule of the language is broken
The program starts but crashes when it meets an impossible instruction
The program runs to the end but gives the wrong result, because the reasoning is wrong
The user enters data that is not of the correct data type
q.why: A logic error gives no crash and no error message, just a wrong answer.

q.q: A program runs but calculates the wrong VAT. What type of error is this?
o: Logic error
Syntax error
Execution error
Translation error
q.why: It runs without crashing but gives the wrong answer.

q.q: Which is an execution (run-time) error?
o: Dividing a number by zero while the program runs
Misspelling Console as Consle in the code
Using > instead of >= in an IF condition
Leaving out a closing bracket on a method call
q.why: Division by zero crashes the program as it runs. The others are syntax and logic errors.

q.q: Which is a syntax error?
o: Writing Consle.WriteLine instead of Console.WriteLine
Opening a file that does not exist
Reading scores[10] from a 10-element array
Using the wrong formula to work out an average
q.why: A misspelt keyword breaks the language rules, so the code will not compile.

q.q: Which is a logic error?
o: Using > instead of >= in a condition, so a boundary value is treated wrongly
Leaving out the semicolon at the end of an assignment statement
Running Convert.ToInt32("ten") while the program is running
Leaving out the closing curly bracket at the end of a method
q.why: Wrong comparison operators give wrong results without crashing.

q.q: When is a syntax error detected?
o: Only when the user enters invalid data
Only during testing with extreme data
After the program has finished running
When the code is translated, before it can run
q.why: The translator rejects code that breaks the rules.

q.q: How is an execution error usually first noticed?
o: A wavy red line appears under the code as it is typed
The program stops while running and shows an exception message
The program runs to the end but the total is wrong
The compiler lists it with a line number before the program runs
q.why: Execution errors are found when they happen, as the program crashes.

q.q: How are logic errors usually found?
o: By the compiler, which lists them with their line numbers
By the program crashing with an exception message
By testing against expected results, dry runs, trace tables and breakpoints
By error underlining in the IDE as the code is typed
q.why: Logic errors produce no message, so the programmer must compare actual with expected results.

q.q: A program reads scores[10] from an array of 10 elements. What type of error results?
o: Syntax error
Logic error
Validation error
Execution error
q.why: Index 10 does not exist in a 10-element array (0 to 9), so the program crashes as it runs.

q.q: A program runs Convert.ToInt32("ten"). What type of error results?
o: Syntax error
Execution error
Logic error
Overflow error
q.why: The code is valid C#, but the conversion fails at run time.

q.q: In C#, if (x = 5) is written instead of if (x == 5). What type of error is this?
o: Logic error
Execution error
Type check error
Syntax error
q.why: The notes list if (x = 5) as a syntax error in C#; the code will not compile.

q.q: A pupil says "A logic error stops the program and gives an error message." What is wrong with this?
o: A logic error stops the program but gives no message; only syntax errors give messages
A logic error lets the program run to the end; stopping with a message describes an execution error
Nothing is wrong; logic errors and execution errors are the same thing
A logic error stops the program before it starts; only execution errors run
q.why: This is the most common confusion between the error types.
Division happens first: c / 3 = 26 with integer division, then 70 + 65 + 26 = 161.

o: double average = (a + b + c) / 3;
double average = (a + b + c) / 3.0;
double average = a + b + (c / 3.0);
int average = (a + b + c) / 3;
q.why: Brackets make the addition happen first, and 3.0 avoids integer division. (a + b + c) / 3 would give 71.

q.q: In the average program, a + b + c / 3 gives 161 instead of 71.666… Why does the program not show an error?
o: The compiler fixes the formula automatically, but gets it wrong
Error messages are only shown for programs that use arrays
The error message is hidden because average is a double
The code follows the language rules and does not crash; the reasoning is simply wrong
q.why: This is a logic error: no crash and no message, just a wrong answer.

q.q: A program compiles with 12 error messages after one change. What is the best first step?
o: Fix the first error first, as one missing bracket can cause several messages
Fix the last error first, as it is closest to the end of the program
Ignore the messages and run the program to see what happens
Delete every line mentioned in an error message
q.why: One mistake can trigger several messages, so start with the first.

q.q: What is debugging?
o: Translating source code into machine code
Checking that input data obeys set rules
Finding and removing errors from a program
Writing comments to explain how the code works
q.why: Debugging is the name for finding and removing errors.

q.q: What does a breakpoint let a programmer do?
o: Stop the program compiling until all errors are fixed
Pause the program at a chosen line and inspect the variables
Skip a line of code that contains a syntax error
Mark the end of a loop so it does not repeat
q.why: A breakpoint pauses execution so you can step through and watch values.

q.q: In Visual Studio, what does the Locals window show while the program is paused at a breakpoint?
o: A list of syntax errors with their line numbers
The machine code produced by the compiler
Every variable with its current value
The files that make up the project
q.why: The Locals window lists each variable and its value; you can even change a value to try something out.

q.q: A programmer steps through code with F10 while comparing variables with a trace table. Where is the logic error most likely to be?
o: At the first line of the program, where variables are declared
At the last line of the program, where the output is shown
At any line underlined in red by the IDE
At the line where the values first stop matching what the trace table says they should be
q.why: The first point of mismatch shows where the logic goes wrong.

q.q: Which IDE features help to prevent and reveal syntax errors?
o: Breakpoints, stepping and the Locals window
Syntax highlighting, error underlining and auto-complete
Trace tables, dry runs and written test plans
try … catch blocks and WHILE validation loops
q.why: These editing features catch rule-breaking code as you type. Breakpoints are for logic errors.

q.q: Why should a programmer change one thing at a time and retest after every fix?
o: So the compiler has fewer lines to translate each time
So the program does not need to be tested at the end
So it is clear which change fixed the problem, or caused a new one
So the error messages are shown in the right order
q.why: Making one change at a time keeps cause and effect clear.

q.q: Which testing approach helps to find logic errors by making sure every path through the code is run?
o: Testing only with normal data that the program is expected to handle
Testing with valid, invalid and extreme data and comparing actual with expected outcomes
Compiling the program several times to see if new errors appear
Running the program once and checking that it does not crash
q.why: Varied test data executes every path, and comparing outcomes reveals wrong results.

q.q: How can validation and error trapping help with execution errors?
o: They turn execution errors into syntax errors so the compiler finds them
They find logic errors by comparing outputs with expected results
They stop many execution errors happening at all
They correct the program's source code automatically
q.why: Checking input and trapping exceptions prevents many crashes.

q.q: In a 6-mark question on error types, what should be given for each type to reach the top level?
o: A definition, an example and how it is detected and dealt with
A definition only, written as clearly as possible
An example only, written in C#
A list of as many examples as possible without definitions
q.why: Cover each error type with definition, example and detection, using technical terms.

q.q: A program to find the largest of three numbers always outputs the first number, even when it is not the largest. No error message appears. What type of error is this?
o: Logic error
Syntax error
Execution error
Type check error
q.why: The program runs to the end without a message but gives the wrong result.

q.q: A program stops with the message "Index was outside the bounds of the array." What type of error is this?
o: Execution error
Syntax error
Logic error
Validation error
q.why: The program translated and started, then crashed while running.

q.q: A programmer forgets the closing ) in Console.WriteLine("Hello";. When will the error be found?
o: When the code is translated, so it will not run
When the program runs and reaches that line
Only when the output is checked against the expected result
Only when a breakpoint is placed on that line
q.why: A missing bracket is a syntax error, found by the translator before the program can run.

q.q: A loop meant to add up ten marks puts the OUTPUT total line inside the loop, so a total is shown ten times. What type of error is this?
o: Syntax error
Execution error
Logic error
Format error
q.why: The notes list 'output inside a loop' as a logic error: the code runs but behaves wrongly.

q.q: Which tool is the best choice for finding an execution error that happens only with certain data?
o: Syntax highlighting in the editor
Auto-complete while typing
Reading the code's comments
Testing with valid, invalid and extreme data
q.why: Varied test data makes the program run the paths that crash; editing features only help with syntax.

q.q: What is error trapping?
o: Detecting a run-time error and handling it so the program does not crash
Checking that input data follows rules before it is used
Testing every path through the code with test data
Removing syntax errors before the program is compiled
q.why: Error trapping deals with exceptions while the program runs.

q.q: In C#, what happens when an execution error occurs?
o: The program throws a syntax error
The compiler stops and lists the error
The program skips the line and carries on
The program throws an exception
q.why: An exception is thrown (or raised); if nothing handles it, the program crashes.

q.q: What is an unhandled exception?
o: An exception that is caught by a catch block and then handled
A syntax error that the compiler did not find before the program ran
A logic error that produces the wrong output but no error message
An exception that no code catches, so it stops the program with an error message
q.why: Unhandled exceptions crash the program.

q.q: Your textbook says an exception is "raised". What word do these notes use for the same thing?
o: Caught
Trapped
Handled
Thrown
q.why: Thrown and raised mean the same thing. Catching is what the catch block does.

q.q: In C#, which block contains the code that might fail?
o: catch
throw
try
finally
q.why: Statements that might fail go inside the try block.

q.q: In C#, which block contains the code that runs when an exception is caught?
o: try
throw
catch
else
q.why: The catch block handles the exception.

q.q: An exception is thrown halfway through a try block. What happens to the rest of the try block?
o: It still runs, and then the catch block runs
It is skipped, and the matching catch block runs
It runs again from the start of the try block
It is skipped, and the program ends immediately
q.why: After an exception the rest of try is skipped and control goes to the matching catch.

q.q: What happens to the catch blocks if nothing goes wrong in the try block?
o: They all run in order
Only the first one runs
The program crashes
They are skipped
q.why: catch blocks only run when an exception is thrown.

q.q: Which exception occurs when Convert.ToInt32 is given "ten"?
o: DivideByZeroException
FileNotFoundException
FormatException
IndexOutOfRangeException
q.why: The text is not in a valid number format.

q.q: Which exception occurs when an integer is divided by zero?
o: FormatException
OverflowException
DivideByZeroException
IndexOutOfRangeException
q.why: Dividing by zero throws DivideByZeroException.

q.q: Which exception occurs when a program tries to open a file that does not exist?
o: FileNotFoundException
FormatException
IndexOutOfRangeException
DivideByZeroException
q.why: A missing file throws FileNotFoundException.

q.q: Which exception occurs when a program reads scores[10] from a 10-element array?
o: FormatException
FileNotFoundException
DivideByZeroException
IndexOutOfRangeException
q.why: Index 10 is outside the range 0 to 9.

q.q: In the points-per-match program, the user types 30 for points and 0 for matches. What is output?
o: Please type whole numbers only. then Program continues...
Points per match: 0 then Program continues...
Matches played cannot be 0. then Program continues...
The program crashes with an unhandled exception
q.why: points / matches throws DivideByZeroException, which is caught; the program then carries on.

q.q: In the points-per-match program, the user types "lots" for points. What is output?
o: Matches played cannot be 0. then Program continues...
The program crashes, as the error is in the first line of try
Please type whole numbers only. then Program continues...
Points per match: 0 then Program continues...
q.why: Convert.ToInt32("lots") throws FormatException; the rest of try, including the matches prompt, is skipped.

q.q: In the points-per-match program, the user types 30 and 6. What is output?
o: Points per match: 5 only
Points per match: 5 then Program continues...
Matches played cannot be 0. then Program continues...
Program continues... only
q.why: No exception is thrown, so the catch blocks are skipped and the line after them still runs.

q.q: Why can a try block have several catch blocks?
o: So different exceptions, such as FormatException and DivideByZeroException, can each get their own response
So the same exception can be handled several times in a row
So the program can try the same code several times
So the compiler can find more syntax errors
q.why: Each catch block handles a different exception type with a suitable message.

q.q: In the age input loop, valid starts false and is set to true straight after Convert.ToInt32 succeeds. The user types "abc", then "15". What happens?
o: The error message is shown twice, then the loop ends
The error message is shown once, then 15 is accepted and the loop ends
15 is rejected because the loop has already run once
The program crashes on "abc" because the loop cannot catch exceptions
q.why: "abc" throws FormatException, so valid stays false; "15" converts and valid becomes true.

q.q: In the age input loop, why is valid = true; placed after the Convert.ToInt32 line inside the try block?
o: So that valid is set to true even when the conversion fails
If the conversion fails, the exception skips that line, so valid stays false and the loop repeats
So the catch block can set valid back to false
Because C# does not allow assignments before a conversion
q.why: The rest of try is skipped after an exception, so valid only becomes true for good input.

q.q: Why is combining try … catch with a loop useful?
o: The loop makes the code inside the try block run more quickly
A catch block is only allowed to be written inside a loop in C#
The loop removes the need to show the user any error message
The user can keep trying until the input works, instead of the program ending
q.why: A loop lets the program recover and ask again.

q.q: How does error trapping make a program more robust?
o: The program runs faster because any lines with errors are skipped
The program no longer needs to be tested before it is released
The program does not crash, so it can keep running and recover from problems
The program can no longer contain any logic errors or wrong outputs
q.why: Robustness means coping with errors without crashing.

q.q: Which is a benefit of error trapping for the user?
o: They never have to enter data again
They get a clear message explaining what went wrong and how to fix it
They can see the program's source code when an error happens
They are shown the exception name and line number
q.why: A helpful message replaces a crash, and work entered so far is not lost.

q.q: How do validation and error trapping work together?
o: Validation catches problems at run time; error trapping checks data follows the rules
Validation checks that data follows the rules; error trapping catches problems that still occur at run time, such as a missing file
Validation finds syntax errors; error trapping finds logic errors
They do the same job, so a program only needs one of them
q.why: They complement each other: a missing file passes validation but is caught by error trapping.

q.q: A program reads from a file that may have been deleted. Which approach stops the program crashing?
o: Add a presence check on the file name typed by the user
Add a breakpoint on the line that opens the file
Use a FOR loop to open the file several times
Put the file-reading code in a try block with a catch for FileNotFoundException
q.why: Error trapping catches the run-time error; a presence check only tests that a name was typed.

q.q: Which is the best description of error trapping for a full-mark answer?
o: It detects a run-time error using try … catch and shows a message or recovers instead of crashing
It is when the program checks that data is the right type, length and format
It is when errors are trapped so the program works properly
It is when the programmer finds errors using a trace table
q.why: A full answer says what it is, how it is done and what happens instead of a crash.

q.q: A program asks for a quantity and must not crash if letters are typed. Which pair of techniques could each achieve this?
o: A presence check, or a breakpoint on the input line
A length check, or Convert.ToInt32 without any error trapping
int.TryParse in a validation loop, or Convert.ToInt32 inside try … catch (FormatException)
A trace table, or syntax highlighting in the IDE
q.why: Both TryParse and try … catch stop letters causing a crash.

q.q: Which part of a try … catch handles the situation where no exception is thrown?
o: The rest of the try block runs and the catch blocks are skipped
The first catch block runs anyway as a check
The program jumps back to the start of the try block
The finally keyword must be used to continue
q.why: When nothing goes wrong, all of try runs and catch is skipped.

q.q: What does it mean to say a program "recovers" from an error?
o: It restarts from the beginning and deletes all the data entered
It deals with the problem, for example by asking again or creating a missing file, and carries on
It shows the exception message and then ends
It ignores the error and outputs whatever value it has
q.why: Recovery means handling the error and continuing.

q.q: Which statement about exceptions is correct?
o: Every exception is caught automatically by C#, so programs never crash
Exceptions are only thrown while the program is being compiled
An exception that is caught can be handled with a message, but an uncaught one crashes the program
An exception is another name for a logic error
q.why: Exceptions happen at run time; uncaught ones crash the program.

q.q: Which keyword starts the block that handles a FormatException in C#?
o: try
catch
throw
handle
q.why: catch (FormatException) { … } handles that exception.

q.q: Which word describes a program that copes with errors and unexpected input without crashing?
o: Efficient
Robust
Compiled
Validated
q.why: Robustness is improved by error trapping.

q.q: A program opens a file of scores. The file has been deleted. Without error trapping, what happens?
o: The program creates an empty file and carries on
The compiler refuses to translate the program
An unhandled exception crashes the program
The program outputs a total of zero and ends normally
q.why: Opening a missing file throws FileNotFoundException; if nothing catches it, the program crashes.

q.q: Which error type is error trapping designed to deal with?
o: Syntax errors
Logic errors
Execution errors
Spelling errors in comments
q.why: try … catch handles exceptions thrown while the program runs; it cannot fix syntax or logic errors.
